title: Theme Toggle
answer: decide and visualize pages get a **light and dark button** that remembers your choice, and decide's build check now reads a page with three scripts.

changes.title: A button switches light and dark
changes.what: Both pages get a round button in the corner. It sets `data-theme` on the page and saves the choice in the browser under `happyface-theme`.
changes.before: Pages followed the system theme, with no way to switch.
changes.after: One click switches; picking the system's own theme follows the system again.

risk.t: The two pages carry the same script, so a fix to one must be copied to the other.

code.note: visualize's page gets the same script.

notes.t: Choosing the theme the system already uses removes the override, so the page follows the system again.

changes.title: decide's syntax check joins every script
changes.what: The build checks the page's scripts by joining them into one file for `node --check`. It joined only the first boundary between them.
changes.why: The new theme script makes three script blocks, so two boundaries.
changes.before: A page with a third script would fail the build's syntax check.
changes.after: Every boundary is joined, so all three scripts check as one.

notes.t: `replaceAll`: a plain `replace` stops at the first match.

review.heading: Read the follow rule, then the one-word fix
review.say: Two small changes; the second exists because of the first.

first.t: When the override is set, kept or cleared.
Every script boundary is joined before the check.

risks.sub: decide and visualize each hold the toggle.

unchecked: A host page that sets `data-theme` itself, such as a published artifact.
